class.name: TerrainMaterialLayer
class.brief_description: One surface of a [TerrainMaterial3D]: rock, scree, soil, alluvium or sand.
class.description: Textures, tint, tiling and porosity of one ground surface. Every texture is optional; without textures the layer is its [member color] and [member roughness]. Textures are sampled in world space, so they never stretch over the terrain's mesh.

method.name: get_albedo_mean
method.description: Mean linear colour of [member albedo_texture], or white without one. Cached until the texture changes.

method.name: get_roughness_mean
method.description: Mean of [member roughness_texture]'s green channel, or [code]1.0[/code] without one. Cached until the texture changes.

members.member: Colour texture, multiplied by [member color]. See [member detail_only].

If [code]true[/code], [member albedo_texture] and [member roughness_texture] are divided by their own means, so they add detail only: the layer keeps the average colour of [member color] and the average [member roughness]. Use it with scanned textures, whose colours and roughness follow no common scale, so every scan matches the palette. If [code]false[/code], the textures are used as they are, multiplied by [member color] and [member roughness].
Height texture (red channel) used for height blending: where two layers meet, the higher one wins, so stones poke through sand instead of fading into it.
How much the layer darkens and smooths when wet (see [member BaseMaterial3D.wetness_porosity]).
Roughness, multiplied by [member roughness_texture]'s green channel.
Roughness texture (green channel), multiplied by [member roughness]. See [member detail_only].
Size in metres one repeat of the textures covers.
